text:
emma: Heads-up — RocketFlow hit token/s SLO alerts this morning, getting a lot of 429s and burst_credit_exhausted in the logs. Customer says it was a short spike from a marketing send. Can someone pick this up? :eyes:

kai: On it. Do we have their dedicated pool id and current burst credits?

emma: pool: df-prod-eu-3, account: rocketflow, logs attached by support ticket. They said autoscale didn't kick for ~90s.

devin: I pulled some logs — admission control started rejecting at 05:12:07 UTC with:

```
admission_controller.go:237 admission: reject request: reason=burst_credit_exhausted pool=df-prod-eu-3 tokens=12000 tps=300
```

sanjay: Also seeing repeated KV cache thrashing around that window which could explain longer tails. spike had many long-sequence requests (1.5k tokens).

ops-bot: [alert] rocketflow: DedicatedPool(df-prod-eu-3) throttle_slo_violation at 2026-03-12T05:12:09Z. burst_credits=0 => triggering fallback policy.

kai: Can you paste the autoscaler events? I want to confirm why no new replicas came up.

devin: kubectl events show: `ScaledUp` event at 05:13:40 but node provisioning lagged. Here's a snippet:

```
Events:
  Type    Reason         Age   From                Message
  ----    ------         ----  ----                -------
  Normal  TriggeredScale  5m    dedicated-autoscaler  Desired replicas: 6 -> 10
  Normal  ScaledUp       3m    k8s-provisioner       Scaling completed
```

kai: So autoscaler decided to scale but cloud provider VM allocation added ~70s. In that gap admission control enforced hard TPS cap.

emma: Customer timeline: spike started at 05:11:55, first 429s at 05:12:07, resolved by ~05:13:45 when new capacity finished boot.

sanjay: Repro steps from our side for engineering run:
1) Use loadgen hitting df-prod-eu-3 endpoint.
2) Burst for 90s at 400 TPS with ~1.2k token avg per request.
3) Observe admission_controller metrics and burst_credit counter.

Command: `./loadgen --host https://api.redwood.example --pool df-prod-eu-3 --concurrency 200 --rtokens 1200 --duration 90s --burst`

devin: Quick mitigation for RocketFlow: enable short-term headroom by bumping min_replicas to 8 and allocate +30% burst credit for next 24h. Also suggest prewarm/launch window for known marketing blasts.

kai: Agreed. I'll open an internal runbook item: increase min_replicas for suspected campaigns and proactively set spike window. Also add a dashboard alert for queue_latency > 200ms and burst_credits < 500.

emma: Sent the mitigation plan to RocketFlow (apply min_replicas=8 for 24h + grant 50k burst credits). They asked why autoscale didn't protect them. Suggest we explain node provisioning delay and admission control tradeoffs.

devin: Action items:
- kai: create PR to add autoscaler prewarm feature flag + runbook (ETA EOD)
- sanjay: investigate KV cache contention and whether long sequences cause disproportionate token drain (ETA 48h)
- ops-bot: schedule temporary burst_credit grant and note in ticket

ops-bot: [action] burst_credit_adjustment applied: +50000 to rocketflow for 24h. ticket=SF-3421

kai: For longer-term: we should consider soft admission (queued buffering) for ephemeral spikes instead of immediate rejects, with SLA implications. I'll sketch options in eng-runtime backlog.

emma: For the support ticket, include repro commands, logs snippet, and the autoscaler event window. I'll mark ticket as high priority until postmortem done. :white_check_mark:

devin: One more note — add a small telemetry patch to log `request_seq_len` in admission metrics so we can correlate sequence length vs credit burn. I'll propose in PR today.

sanjay: Confirmed I can recreate similar 429 pattern in staging with loadgen. Will attach staging traces to the postmortem.

emma: Great. Closing the immediate escalation; keeping thread open for follow-ups.
